paper.title: Breaking the $\sqrt{T}$ Barrier: Instance-Independent Logarithmic Regret in Stochastic Contextual Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandit with linear payoffs (stochastic contexts)
unmapped: K context vectors per round drawn independently of the past and of each other, supported on [-c/sqrt(d), c/sqrt(d)]^d, conditional mean zero, conditional covariance >= rho_min I, and (z^T beta)^2 conditionally sub-Gaussian with variance <= 4 rho_min
the learner knows rho_min (used to set the initial epoch length T_1 and the confidence radius)
settings.definition_quote: At the beginning of each round $t \in [T]$, the learner chooses one of the $K$ available arms, and gets a reward. ... the learner is handed $K$ context vectors, $d$ dimensional each ... the reward obtained is given by $\langle \beta_{i,t}, \theta^* \rangle + \xi_t$, where ... $\|\theta^*\| \leq 1$ ... $\mathbb{E}_{t-1}[\beta_{i,t}] = 0 \qquad \mathbb{E}_{t-1} [\beta_{i,t} \, \beta_{i,t}^\top] \succeq \rho_{\min} I.$

algorithms.name: OFUL of Chatterji et al. (variant without arm biases)

bound.regime: d >= C_1 (log T / log log T) log(K^2/delta)

symbols.rho_min: lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the conditional context covariance
symbols.Lambda: (1/log log T) * log(rho_min^2 T / (d^2 log^4(KT/delta) log(dT/delta)))
symbols.frakT: log^3(K d^2 log T log^4(KT/delta) log(dT/delta)/(rho_min^2 delta)) * log^2(d^3 log T log^4(KT/delta) log(dT/delta)/(rho_min^2 delta))

conditions: contexts satisfy the stochastic assumptions (zero mean, covariance >= rho_min I, bounded in [-c/sqrt(d), c/sqrt(d)]^d)
d >= C_1 (log T / log log T) log(K^2/delta)
the analysis uses a shift-robustness lemma that assumes contexts i.i.d. across time and arms

source.label: thm:main_theorem

results.notes: Holds with probability at least 1 - c*delta. The regret is defined through means, max_j <beta_jt, theta*> - <beta_Bt, theta*>, against the best arm in each round.

bound.regime: d >= C_1 (log T / log log T) log(K^2/delta)

conditions: contexts drawn from Unif[-c_0/sqrt(d), c_0/sqrt(d)]^d (rho_min = c_1/d)
d >= C_1 (log T / log log T) log(K^2/delta)

source.quote: Suppose the initial phase length $T_1 = \Tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^4)$ and $d \geq C_1 \frac{\log T}{\log \log T} \log (K^2/\delta)$. Playing Algorithm~\ref{algo:main_algo} for $T$ times incur a regret of $R(T) \leq \mathcal{O} ( d^3 \polylog(T,K,d, \delta) )$, with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Special case of Theorem 5.1 with uniform contexts. The polylog factor in T, K, d and delta is absorbed into O_tilde.

symbols.theta_norm: ||theta*||, the norm of the unknown parameter
symbols.delta_1: confidence parameter; the bound holds w.p. >= 1 - 18 delta_1 - delta_s
symbols.delta_s: confidence parameter of the initial norm estimate

conditions: T large enough that 2 C sigma sqrt(d) T^(-1/4) log(K sqrt(T)/delta_1) <= 1 (from Lemma B.2)

source.label: cor:alb_norm_improved
source.quote: The regret of Algorithm \ref{algo:alb_norm} at the end of $T$ time-steps satisfies with probability at-least $1- 18\delta_1 - \delta_s$, $R(T) \leq C\|\theta^*\|(\sqrt{K}+\sqrt{d})\sqrt{T}\log\left(\frac{KT}{\delta_1}\right)$, where $C$ is an universal constant.

results.notes: Stated as a corollary of Theorem 1 of Ghosh et al. (2021), obtained by recomputing that paper's Lemma 1 for the modified algorithm. Holds with probability at least 1 - 18*delta_1 - delta_s.
